The Direction - the law stops being prose

Wave 22 proved the law slice by slice, by hand. Five verbs stopped lying because five builders each went looking. That does not scale and it does not hold: nothing in the repo prevents the ninety-fifth checkmark from being printed on an exit code tomorrow. Wave 23's identity is that the law gets TEETH - it becomes a thing the repo enforces rather than a thing a wave remembers.

What the finished experience feels like: an operator types bp cloud deploy staging and the verb tells the truth about what is running. Four named outcomes, never a bare tick - ADVANCED (the box now serves <sha>, was <old>), STALL (the run exited 0 but the box is still serving <old>, a named non-zero failure), ALREADY AT <sha> (a coalesce, not a deploy), and UNPERFORMABLE (the read-back could not run, stated in the same breath, never dressed as success). That is the Kinsta/Vercel bar: a deploy that reports what the box IS, not what the command DID.
Four tracks, in this order of priority:

items.value: DEPLOY, the flagship - pds-w22-deploy-readback. The dependency has merged; this is the epic's headline success-lie and it goes first. The design crux the surveyors must settle: the verb deploys a REF, the box serves a SHA, so the honest comparison is a BEFORE/AFTER read of /status.json - advance is observable without resolving the ref at all - reinforced by a ref-to-sha resolution wherever one is available.

CENSUS plus GUARD - 94 checkmark prints live in internal/cli alone, plus the Elixir receipts and the shell scripts. Census them all, classify each as backed / unbacked / structurally unbackable, fix the worst remote-state claims, and land a guard proven BY MUTATION: delete a read-back and the guard must red. If an honest guard cannot be built at reasonable cost it degrades to a census document with per-site evidence and NO gate - and says so. A green that means nothing is the exact defect this epic exists to kill.

content.value: The sharpest attack on the winner

The guard is the wave's own success-lie. A registry of "classified" call sites passes CI by containing a non-empty string - precisely the shape this epic exists to destroy, shipped by the epic itself. A builder under time pressure registers a site as backed, the gate goes green, and wave 24 inherits a green that means nothing. This is not hypothetical: PDS-D298 exists because a sibling epic CLAIMED 45 parks carried reasons and re-derivation found ZERO, and PDS-D306 exists because wave 22 lost 19 of its own adjudications inside the very wave that wrote the rule against it.
How the wave absorbs it - three clauses, all binding on the guard slice:

items.value: The guard NEVER accepts a classification string as evidence. A site claiming to be backed must be structurally backed: its success print reachable only through a named read-back, with a test that exercises the mismatch branch.

The guard is proven BY MUTATION or it does not ship. Delete the read-back, run the gate, the gate must red - that transcript is the criterion evidence. "Make the check able to fail" is repo doctrine and it applies hardest to a check about honesty.

The guard is SCOPED, not universal - only verbs claiming a REMOTE state change. A local claim such as "config written" self-points and earns no entry; a universal registry maximises exactly the string-passing failure mode. If the surveyors find no honest guard shape at reasonable cost, the slice ships a census DOCUMENT with per-site evidence and no gate, and states plainly that the law remains unenforced. Refusing to ship a fake green is a successful outcome for this slice.

PDS Wave 23 - The Law Gets Teeth: finish the read-back, census the rest, pay the debts

Living wave Paper for wave 23 of the Personal Development Server epic (epic task task-2ac1f95237c4a8e5). Charter: .claude/workflows/bp-pds-charter.md, read from origin/main @ a8c767dbd (4,480 lines, D1-D308). Prior wave Paper: pds-wave-22-2026-07-27 - "Success Must Be Observable", 7 slices merged, grade B+. Every later phase appends here; someone opening this mid-wave sees exactly where the wave stands.

Where this wave stands
Phase: STRATEGIZE complete - 17 broad surveyors about to fly. Wave 22 ratified the law and proved it on five verbs. Wave 23 finishes the slice wave 22 deferred by name, generalises the law past the rows already filed, and pays the eight debts wave 22 measured. The crown is SEALED 12/12 and CLOSED - it will not be re-fired.

The Wish

Run PDS wave 23 - the wave that finishes what wave 22 started and drives the backlog down honestly. Wave 22 ratified the epic's law and every slice must still obey it: NO BARKPARK VERB MAY REPORT SUCCESS ON AN EXIT CODE ALONE. Every success claim must be backed by a post-condition READ of the state it claims to have produced, and any claim it cannot back must say so in the same breath.

Round 1 starts with the slice wave 22 deferred BY NAME, now unblocked: pds-w22-deploy-readback. Then, in priority order: (1) census the REMAINING success-lies - the law generalises past the rows already filed; (2) the 8 backlog rows wave 22 filed with measured evidence; (3) continue the triage against main under the same proof standard - after every disposition write, RE-READ the row and COUNT the field you claimed to write. No crown re-fire; no new capability invented to avoid finishing the ones that exist.

Ground truth - premise smoke, run not assumed

Every premise this direction rests on was git-shown against origin/main @ a8c767dbd before it was allowed to carry weight. A citation nobody ran is a phantom wearing a number.

Epic ledger, re-derived this hour from bp task get task-2ac1f95237c4a8e5: 157 children - 80 open, 58 done, 10 considering, 9 cancelled. Wave 22's "~124 open" (PDS-D307) counts the wider epic scope; the direct-child figure is 80. Any number this wave quotes must name the query that produced it.

The Direction - the law stops being prose

Wave 22 proved the law slice by slice, by hand. Five verbs stopped lying because five builders each went looking. That does not scale and it does not hold: nothing in the repo prevents the ninety-fifth checkmark from being printed on an exit code tomorrow. Wave 23's identity is that the law gets TEETH - it becomes a thing the repo enforces rather than a thing a wave remembers.

What the finished experience feels like: an operator types bp cloud deploy staging and the verb tells the truth about what is running. Four named outcomes, never a bare tick - ADVANCED (the box now serves <sha>, was <old>), STALL (the run exited 0 but the box is still serving <old>, a named non-zero failure), ALREADY AT <sha> (a coalesce, not a deploy), and UNPERFORMABLE (the read-back could not run, stated in the same breath, never dressed as success). That is the Kinsta/Vercel bar: a deploy that reports what the box IS, not what the command DID.

Four tracks, in this order of priority:

  1. DEPLOY, the flagship - pds-w22-deploy-readback. The dependency has merged; this is the epic's headline success-lie and it goes first. The design crux the surveyors must settle: the verb deploys a REF, the box serves a SHA, so the honest comparison is a BEFORE/AFTER read of /status.json - advance is observable without resolving the ref at all - reinforced by a ref-to-sha resolution wherever one is available.
  2. CENSUS plus GUARD - 94 checkmark prints live in internal/cli alone, plus the Elixir receipts and the shell scripts. Census them all, classify each as backed / unbacked / structurally unbackable, fix the worst remote-state claims, and land a guard proven BY MUTATION: delete a read-back and the guard must red. If an honest guard cannot be built at reasonable cost it degrades to a census document with per-site evidence and NO gate - and says so. A green that means nothing is the exact defect this epic exists to kill.
  3. DEBTS - the eight rows wave 22 filed with measured evidence, highest value first: pds-bl-bounded-import-unpack (spill-to-disk extract; the measured bound is 1x the LARGEST MEMBER = 1.31 GB today, never write "constant memory"), pds-bl-blob-storage-readback (the receipt says bytes RECEIVED, never STORED), pds-bl-crown-launch-armed-without-liveness, pds-bl-scratch-teardown-strands-the-survivor, pds-bl-owner-walk-reaches-the-mint, pds-bl-close-audit-gaps, pds-bl-task-events-carry-no-worker, pds-bl-tickets-local-otp28-divergence.
  4. LEDGER - fix the evaporation defect at its SOURCE (pds-bl-park-note-evaporates: 19 of 23 adjudications lost within hours, all 31 affected rows carrying a content.github key, consistent with a reconciler rebuilding content wholesale). Then continue the triage under D298's re-read proof and D306's ruling that disposition_reason is the durable field. A convention that survives only because everyone remembers it is the ledger's own success-lie.

Fence: api/**, internal/**, deploy/**, scripts/pds-*, and the pds-* ledger namespace. cloud/** is fenced OUT this wave - a concurrent Cloud Console hardening wave holds it and the gr-*/cch-* namespace.

The Direction Debate

Three directions were developed far enough to be attacked, not sketched to be dismissed.

A - PURE BURN-DOWNNo meta-machinery. Deploy read-back, then the eight debts, then triage as many rows as hands allow. Maximum rows moved per builder-hour.LOST. It is the fastest wave and the shortest-lived one: wave 24 hunts lies by hand again, from zero, because the law stays prose. Wave 22 already ran this play and its own debrief predicts the census will surface lies nobody has filed - and a burn-down cannot surface what nobody filed.
B - GUARD FIRSTBuild the enforcement machinery, defer the debts. Every success claim in the repo gets a registry entry and a CI gate; rows wait for wave 24.LOST. It pays no named debt, and the wish forbids exactly this move: do not invent a new capability to avoid finishing the ones that exist. Worse, a registry is the easiest success-lie in the wave - see the attack below.
C - LEDGER FIRSTTreat wave 22's own failure as the headline: fix the evaporation defect, make dispositions durable at the server, then triage the whole open set to a clean state before touching product code.LOST on sequencing, ABSORBED as track 4. It is right that the ledger is this epic's spine and that losing 19 adjudications is the wave's own failure class. But it leaves the epic's flagship product lie - a deploy verb that cannot tell you what the box is running - standing for another wave, while the dependency that unblocks it sits merged on main.
WINNER - THE LAW GETS TEETHDeploy read-back flagship; census plus mutation-proven guard; the eight measured debts; ledger durability and triage. Synthesis, ordered by what an unattended owner feels first.WON because it is the only candidate that makes wave 23 the LAST wave that has to hand-hunt this defect class, while still paying every debt wave 22 measured. It takes A's rows, B's leverage and C's spine, and sequences them by owner-visible harm.

The sharpest attack on the winner

The guard is the wave's own success-lie. A registry of "classified" call sites passes CI by containing a non-empty string - precisely the shape this epic exists to destroy, shipped by the epic itself. A builder under time pressure registers a site as backed, the gate goes green, and wave 24 inherits a green that means nothing. This is not hypothetical: PDS-D298 exists because a sibling epic CLAIMED 45 parks carried reasons and re-derivation found ZERO, and PDS-D306 exists because wave 22 lost 19 of its own adjudications inside the very wave that wrote the rule against it.

How the wave absorbs it - three clauses, all binding on the guard slice:

  • The guard NEVER accepts a classification string as evidence. A site claiming to be backed must be structurally backed: its success print reachable only through a named read-back, with a test that exercises the mismatch branch.
  • The guard is proven BY MUTATION or it does not ship. Delete the read-back, run the gate, the gate must red - that transcript is the criterion evidence. "Make the check able to fail" is repo doctrine and it applies hardest to a check about honesty.
  • The guard is SCOPED, not universal - only verbs claiming a REMOTE state change. A local claim such as "config written" self-points and earns no entry; a universal registry maximises exactly the string-passing failure mode. If the surveyors find no honest guard shape at reasonable cost, the slice ships a census DOCUMENT with per-site evidence and no gate, and states plainly that the law remains unenforced. Refusing to ship a fake green is a successful outcome for this slice.

Secondary risks, each converted to a survey question

  • The read-back may be UNPERFORMABLE in the field - if a box's status.json commit derives from BuildInfo and the box's checkout is shallow, the served value could be "unknown" (PDS-D304 measured exactly this class locally). Surveys deploy-readback-design and status-json-in-the-field settle it. If it is unperformable everywhere, the slice's fourth outcome becomes its PRIMARY outcome - which is still a win over a bare tick.
  • Fence collision - the concurrent Cloud Console wave holds cloud/**, but internal/cli/cloud_*.go is OURS by directory and THEIRS by name. Survey fence-collision maps it before any builder flies.
  • pds-bl-bounded-import-unpack touches the bundle engine, whose md5-parity suite is the epic's permanent regression tripwire, and PDS-D301 filed it explicitly NOT BUILT. Survey bounded-import-unpack-seam decides whether the pack path's existing spill machinery makes it a safe slice or a wave-25 problem.
  • Guerrilla degrades hard under concurrent waves - capabilities observed at 2.8s to 10.3s and large payloads 500 outright. Every ledger write this wave must be TIGHT, retried with backoff, and re-read before any conclusion. Never conclude a write failed from an exit code - that is the wave's own law pointed at the wave.
  • Any timing or pass/fail number this wave quotes must name the tree it was taken in and the load it was taken under. A lead measurement was refuted 17x on duration this week for exactly that omission.

The Survey Plan - 17 broad assignments

Width now buys precision later. Each surveyor is one Opus at medium effort. Every load-bearing assumption in the stress-test above appears here as a question, so the fleets carry ammunition rather than the direction carrying hedges.

The bar for this wave

Survey digest - 17 reports, coverage complete, zero deficit

Every dispatched surveyor reported. The direction survives on its spine and is REFUTED on three named premises. The flagship is cleaner than filed; the ledger's root cause is not what the wish suspected; and the guard track is constrained by a fence nobody re-read.

DEBRIEF — wave 23 round 1 closed, 2026-07-28, by the wave reviewer

SEVEN OF SEVEN ROUND-1 SLICES BUILT, GATED, REVIEWED, PUSHED AND PR'd — #6548–#6554, plus the charter debrief on #6557. That last clause is the one six previous waves missed: nothing here is sitting on a local-only branch in a shared checkout that another cycle resets. Round 2 (pds-w23-triage-round) is deferred BY DESIGN, not stalled, and is unblocked the moment #6550 merges.

GRADE: A−. Every slice attacks a real, measured lie and refuses the cheap version of its own fix. What keeps it off an A is named in full below: the success-claim registry is thinner than its framing implies, and two slices shipped code paths that are read and not run. Reviewer edits totalled four commits — three fixes to real defects, one test — and every gate was re-run green on the final branch.

What earns the grade, and what costs it

WHAT EARNS IT. Three moments stand out. (1) The blob slice does not merely avoid the File.stat trap — it pins the trap as a passing assertion and then re-proves the bucket is genuinely empty by dropping the cache copy, which is what makes trap 2 a lie rather than a disagreement. (2) The success-claim census CORRECTS THE BRIEF THAT COMMISSIONED IT: told to write down shell non-proof checkmarks = 0 and Elixir console claims = 0, the builder re-measured, got 2 and 1, and shipped the corrected numbers with the correction stated — because writing a number measured to be false would have been that slice's own success-lie. The conclusion the brief wanted survived the correction. (3) The bounded-import slice states 1× the largest member as a BOUND and refuses 'constant memory' even though one sample measured 0.01×. That is the epic's law applied to the epic's own prose.

WHAT COSTS IT, and it is not cosmetic. The success-claim registry is thinner than its framing implies: rows like hzDone and emitDeviceLoginSuccess differ only by an identifier in the fixture, so they prove the render reads its argument, not that the response was a post-condition read. The A1/A2/A3 judgment still lives in prose in the census doc — the exact shape that slice was told to distrust. The builder says so plainly in their own review, which is why this costs a plus rather than a letter. Two slices shipped code paths that are read and not run: the import spill's two new failure branches (Plug.Test cannot answer {:error,_} to read_body, and this suite does not fill a filesystem) and the deploy verb's end-to-end ssh leg. And cmd_arm — the function an operator actually types — is still never executed by any test; only the helper it calls is.

BLOAT: none worth naming. No slice invented a capability to avoid finishing one. AESTHETICS: the receipt copy is genuinely good — 'STALL: the deploy exited 0 but <target> still serves <sha>', 'is STILL pinned', 'INTERRUPTED after N documents — <file> is PARTIAL, do not restore from it' — and the UNPERFORMABLE sentences are distinct per shape rather than one shrug. The counter-example is the wave's own ledger, where six of seven slice rows read lifecycle OPEN on a board while their work is built and PR'd: true to the sweeper, misleading to a human.

Ledger audit

Every built slice was claimed, stamped AS THE WORK HAPPENED (evidence strings carry run output and file:line, not summaries written at the end), and left honest. Across all seven, exactly TWO criteria are open for a non-merge reason and both are stamped as misses with notes: the deploy slice's live-run transcript, and the harness slice's PR statement — which the reviewer then satisfied and stamped, taking that slice to 7/8 (re-read and counted after writing). Every other open criterion is the merge-gated row the LEAD closes on merge. No task outside this wave was touched.

The correction is to the REVIEW phase's own conduct, recorded here rather than silently tidied: the reviewer re-filed that defect under a second id before reading this Paper's own list, then cancelled the duplicate. Nothing else in this Paper is invalidated by a later phase. The direction, the survey digest, the three refuted premises and the decisions all held through the build unchanged.

What the next wave takes

Wave status: COMPLETE. Seven of seven round-1 slices built, reviewed, pushed and PR'd as #6548–#6554; charter debrief on #6557. Grade A−. Round 2 (pds-w23-triage-round) is unblocked the moment #6550 merges. The law now has code enforcing it on the Go CLI, an honest census where it does not, and six verbs that read what they claim.
